title: Reranker quantization profile sweep and ranking-quality validation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Produce production-ready quantization profiles for the reranker model family (rdrk-large/medium) and validate ranking quality using NDCG and MRR so we can ship INT8/FP8 runtime modes with confidence. Scope: calibration pipeline, candidate sampling strategy, per-layer vs per-channel parameterization, evaluation harness and gating criteria. Deliverables: (1) calibration scripts + config templates for FP8 and INT8, (2) canonical calibration dataset and sampling spec, (3) automated eval job that outputs NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, bootstrap confidence intervals, and token-level inference performance numbers, (4) rollout gating rules and canary plan. Experiment matrix: - numeric formats: FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, INT8 (symmetric per-channel), INT8 (asymmetric per-tensor) - activation handling: per-tensor min/max (percentile 99.9, 99.99), KL-divergence-based histogram binning, moving-average dynamic range - calibration set sizes: 1k / 5k / 25k queries - sampling weight: uniform vs query-frequency-weighted vs top-k-candidate-weighted - eval sets: production query distribution (prod-queries-2026-01), long-tail queries subset (tail-queries), and a curated relevance testset (relevance-2025-v3). Calibration design notes: - For INT8 we prefer per-channel symmetric quantization on weights and per-tensor asymmetric for activations when it yields lower KL. - FP8 profiles explore 8-bit float exponent/mantissa tradeoffs; test both e4m3 and e5m2 encodings under same calibration pipeline. - Use KL-divergence over activation histograms (256 bins) to pick clipping thresholds as primary method; fallback to percentile clipping when histograms are low-signal. - Candidate-level KV caching differences must be preserved in calibration runs; enable same KV-seed/control for parity across numeric formats. Accuracy validation: - Primary metrics: NDCG@10 and MRR at top-10. Also track NDCG@1 and @3 for headroom. - Gating thresholds for promoting a quant profile: absolute NDCG@10 drop <= 0.005 (0.5%) compared to float baseline AND relative MRR drop <= 0.01 (1.0%) with 95% bootstrap CI not overlapping negative significance. - Secondary checks: failure cases classified with automated diff toolkit to categorize reranked lists where top-1 flips or core intent changes. - Performance tradeoff target: inference throughput increase >= 1.6x for INT8, >=2.1x for FP8 on our A100 inference pools, and latency P50/P95 within SLA 50ms/200ms for 512-token sequences where applicable. Evaluation infra and artifacts: - All experiments are reproducible via runtimes/quant/calibration-experiments with a single YAML describing dataset, model checkpoint, and profile seed. - Results pushed to the eval dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/reranker-quant/ENG-11234 (internal) - Archived calibration outputs: gs://redwood-prod/quant-calibration/ENG-11234/ - Canonical calibration dataset: gs://redwood-prod/calibration-sets/relevance-2025-v3/ (5k seed, plus replication instructions) Acceptance criteria: - One INT8 profile and one FP8 profile that meet gating criteria on the canonical eval set and pass the tail-queries smoke tests. - Calibration pipeline CI that runs a 1k-sample quick-check on pull requests and a full 5k-run nightly job. - Documentation: Confluence doc with calibration recipes and recommended runtime flags committed (link in attachments). Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (dev): internal runs + PR validation (already started). - Stage 2 (staging canary): deploy INT8 profile to 5% of reranker traffic for 48h with dual-write logging to compare ranking deltas. - Stage 3 (production): if canary passes gates, expand to 50% then 100% over a week with rollback triggers on NDCG/MRR degradation or error rate regressions. Operational controls: - Feature flag: reranker_quant_profile_v2 - Monitoring: daily NDCG baseline drift, per-customer rerank regressions, increased stderr/throw rates. - Automatic rollback hooks in Console if customer_impact > medium or if error rates spike +2x in 30 minutes.
